Increment

/IN-kruh-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Increment means a small, regular increase or addition; the process of increasing step by step.

Her contract added five hundred dollars to her salary every January — a single increment, small on its own but substantial after a decade of steady steps.

Worked Example

After each lap, the coach raised the target pace by a tiny increment — two seconds per mile — so the runners barely noticed the challenge growing.

The sentence captures what makes an increment an increment: one small, discrete, regular step of increase, repeated on a fixed schedule.

How Increment Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

step

step: A step is any single stage in a progression, while an increment stresses a measured, often numeric, addition.

installment

installment: An installment is one portion of something delivered in parts — usually money or episodes — whereas an increment is one portion of growth.

gradation

gradation: A gradation is one level in a graded series, emphasizing position on a scale more than the act of increasing.

Antonyms

decrement

decrement: A decrement is the exact mirror image: one small, regular step of decrease.

reduction

reduction: A reduction is any lowering in amount, opposing the growth an increment delivers.

How Strong Is It? — uptick → increment → surge

uptick vs. increment

uptick vs. increment: An uptick is an even slighter, often one-off rise, while an increment is a defined step that usually recurs on a schedule.

surge vs. increment

surge vs. increment: A surge is a large, sudden swell of increase — far beyond the small, controlled step that an increment describes.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of increment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: in; into; upon

Root — -cre-

Root — -cre-: to grow (from crescere)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Increment comes straight from Latin incrementum: in- ('upon') plus crescere ('to grow') plus -ment, the suffix that turns a process into a thing. Read the chips in order and you get 'a result of growing upon' — growth stacked on top of what was already there. That stacking image is exactly right: each increment is one more layer added to the pile, small by itself, powerful in accumulation.

Use the root in a new word: crescendo

Use the root in a new word: crescendo: The orchestra built toward a thundering crescendo, its volume growing measure by measure — music's own word for 'growing,' from the same Latin crescere.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Increment is at home in workplaces, science, and computing — salary increments, one-degree increments, incrementing a counter. Keep it distinct from its unit-mate augment: an increment is a noun naming one small, regular step of increase, while augment is a verb for the broader act of enlarging something by adding to it.
